answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a time-limited bond in a scarce token before it may transact. Randomly selected established agents test its work, and proven collusion or contradictory claims slash the bond. Reputation accumulates only from independently sampled successes, so a Sybil operator must fund and wait for every fake identity, while risking the entire batch when one is caught. Calling identities falcon, anchor, or island changes nothing: each still pays the same bond.
